```ts
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { ALERT_KINDS, ALERT_RULES, PUSH_KINDS, type AlertChannelState, type AlertFacts, type AlertKind } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { StaffAlertKind, StaffMessage } from "../auth";
import { createJob, type JobLock } from "../lib/jobs";
import type { ModerationDeps } from "./context";
import { urgentWaiting } from "./repo";

/**
 * Staff alerts (3c design, section 7.12; 3f design, sections 5 and 7.2). Every alert has two legs. The push: one row of
 * alert_outbox, which the watcher (apps/api/src/notify) publishes to the phones with the fixed sentence of its kind,
 * counts and times only. The mail: to every live staff account, with counts and times and, for 3c's and 3e's kinds, the
 * staff handle where they name one; never a link or content. The moderation module, which never sees an address, keeps
 * each alert's throttle as one key of the shared limit store, and the alert tick below writes the time-driven alerts
 * (alert_steps()) and mails every 3f alert whose mail is its push's sentence, whoever wrote its row.
 */

/** The key and the window of the urgent lane's alert. The dispatch job repeats the alert under the same key. */
export const URGENT_ALERT_KEY = "moderation-urgent";
export const URGENT_ALERT_WINDOW_MS = 15 * 60_000;

/** The alert tick's name: its lock is `job:alert-tick`, and its log lines carry it. */
export const ALERT_TICK_JOB = "alert-tick";
/** The time between the end of one round of the tick and the start of the next. */
export const ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS = ALERT_RULES.tickSeconds * 1000;

/**
 * The kinds whose mail is their push's sentence that the tick mails from a row, each a template of the mailer: those a
 * row can hold so far. Every later kind of 3f joins this list in the task that first writes its rows.
 */
export const TICK_MAILED_KINDS: readonly StaffAlertKind[] = [
  "contact_mail",
  "contact_mail_escalated",
  "order_due",
  "mailbox_unreachable",
  "alert_channel_down",
  "order_opened",
  "order_corrected",
  "order_unverified",
  // Task 3.
  "order_effected",
  "order_reinstated",
  "hold_ending",
];

/** A list of the contracts' words as a PostgreSQL array, for `= any(...)`: no word holds a comma or a quote. */
const words = (values: readonly string[]) => sql`${`{${values.join(",")}}`}::text[]`;

/**
 * The facts of an alert's push: the counts and times its kind names in ALERT_KINDS, never a handle, a lane's list or a
 * reason. 3c's and 3e's kinds keep their full message for the mail; the push gets these alone. A 3f alert's message is
 * its facts.
 */
export function alertFacts(message: StaffMessage): AlertFacts {
  switch (message.template) {
    case "moderation_urgent":
      return { count: message.count, oldestAt: message.oldest.toISOString() };
    case "moderation_waiting":
      // What the mail lists, each line's own count: the cases of each lane past its time, the cases that hold a measure
      // taken while deciding, and the replies waiting.
      return { count: message.lanes.reduce((sum, lane) => sum + Math.max(0, lane.count), 0) + message.interim + (message.replies?.count ?? 0) };
    case "moderation_burst":
      return { count: message.count };
    case "moderation_reads":
      return { limit: message.limit };
    case "moderation_reveal":
    case "moderation_csam_lifted":
      return { at: message.at.toISOString() };
    default:
      return message.facts;
  }
}

/** Writes one alert's row, with its kind's priority and scope; the database forces its times and its two legs as owed. */
async function insertAlert(q: Pick<ModerationDeps["apiDb"], "execute">, kind: AlertKind, facts: AlertFacts): Promise<number> {
  const entry = ALERT_KINDS[kind];
  const [row] = await q.execute<{ id: string }>(
    sql`insert into public.alert_outbox (kind, priority, scope, facts) values (${kind}, ${entry.priority}, ${entry.scope}, ${JSON.stringify(facts)}::jsonb) returning id`,
  );
  return Number(row!.id);
}

/**
 * Mails a 3f alert's row once: the row is taken FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED while its mail goes, and marked mailed when an
 * address took it, so staffAlert and the tick never both mail it. Answers how many addresses took it, or "elsewhere" when
 * another holds the row or it was mailed meanwhile.
 */
async function mailClaimed(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "auth">, id: number, message: StaffMessage): Promise<number | "elsewhere"> {
  return deps.apiDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
    const claimed = await tx.execute(sql`select id from public.alert_outbox where id = ${id} and mailed_at is null for update skip locked`);
    if (claimed.length === 0) return "elsewhere";
    const accepted = await deps.auth.mailStaff(message);
    if (accepted > 0) await tx.execute(sql`update public.alert_outbox set mailed_at = now() where id = ${id}`);
    return accepted;
  });
}

/**
 * Sends a staff alert at most once in its key's window (null: no throttle, for a reveal and for a decision that lifted
 * the protection of reported images). After the throttle, in this order: it writes the alert's row of alert_outbox, which
 * the watcher pushes; then it mails every staff account. For 3c's and 3e's kinds (`mail: "own"`) the mail is the caller's
 * full message, and the row is marked mailed whether or not an address took it: the tick never renders such a mail from
 * a row. For a kind of 3f whose mail is its sentence, the row is marked only when an address took the mail, and the tick
 * mails a row left without it.
 *
 * An alert fails open: a row that cannot be written is logged and the mail goes all the same, and when the store cannot
 * be reached both go without a throttle. It answers sent when either leg took the alert. The hit is given back, so the
 * next occasion that meets the alert's condition sends it again, when the mail of one of 3c's and 3e's kinds went to
 * nobody (no row can mail it later), and for a kind of 3f only when neither leg took it. A failed give-back is logged.
 * It never throws for a failed send, which mailStaff logs.
 */
export async function staffAlert(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "auth" | "limits" | "log">, key: string | null, windowMs: number, message: StaffMessage): Promise<"sent" | "throttled" | "unsent"> {
  let counted = false;
  if (key !== null) {
    try {
      const hit = await deps.limits.hit(key, windowMs);
      counted = true;
      if (hit.count > 1) return "throttled";
    } catch (err) {
      deps.log.warn({ err, alert: key }, "moderation alert: the limit store could not be reached; the alert goes without its throttle");
    }
  }
  const kind = message.template;
  const entry = ALERT_KINDS[kind];
  let rowId: number | null = null;
  try {
    // A statement of its own, in a savepoint where the caller holds a transaction: a refused row never aborts it.
    rowId = await deps.apiDb.transaction((tx) => insertAlert(tx, kind, alertFacts(message)));
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.warn({ err, alert: key ?? kind }, "moderation alert: its row for the phones could not be written; the mail goes all the same");
  }
  let accepted: number;
  if (entry.mail === "sentence" && rowId !== null) {
    const mailed = await mailClaimed(deps, rowId, message).catch((err: unknown) => {
      deps.log.warn({ err, alert: rowId }, "moderation alert: its mail could not be sent now; the alert tick sends it");
      return 0;
    });
    accepted = mailed === "elsewhere" ? 1 : mailed;
  } else {
    accepted = await deps.auth.mailStaff(message);
    if (rowId !== null && entry.mail === "own") {
      await deps.apiDb
        .execute(sql`update public.alert_outbox set mailed_at = now() where id = ${rowId}`)
        .catch((err: unknown) => deps.log.warn({ err, alert: rowId }, "moderation alert: its row could not be marked mailed; nothing mails it again"));
    }
  }
  const pushed = rowId !== null && entry.legs.includes("push");
  const giveBack = accepted === 0 && (entry.mail === "own" || !pushed);
  if (giveBack && counted && key !== null) {
    await deps.limits.release(key).catch((err: unknown) => deps.log.warn({ err, alert: key }, "moderation alert: the hit of an alert nobody received could not be given back"));
  }
  return accepted > 0 || pushed ? "sent" : "unsent";
}

/**
 * The urgent lane's alert: when an intake has put an item into lane 0, every staff account is told how many cases wait
 * there and since when the oldest does, and the phone on call is woken. A notice about a post that quotes another puts
 * two cases into the lane and sends one alert that counts both. Best effort, after the commit and the answer; the
 * dispatch job repeats it while a lane-0 item still calls for someone.
 */
export async function alertUrgentLane(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "auth" | "limits" | "log">): Promise<"sent" | "throttled" | "unsent" | "nothing_waiting"> {
  const waiting = await urgentWaiting(deps.apiDb);
  // Decided in the moment between the intake's commit and this read: nothing is left to alert about.
  if (waiting.count === 0 || waiting.oldest === null) return "nothing_waiting";
  return staffAlert(deps, URGENT_ALERT_KEY, URGENT_ALERT_WINDOW_MS, { template: "moderation_urgent", count: waiting.count, oldest: waiting.oldest });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the channel's health

/** The alert channel's state as the console's home and the tick read it, with the time since when. */
export interface ChannelHealth {
  channel: AlertChannelState;
  since: Date | null;
}

/**
 * The channel's state, read fresh (3f design, sections 5 and 7.2 step 3), by the database's clock: `off` with NOTIFY=off;
 * `down` while the watcher's beat is older than channel_down_minutes (or there never was one), or a row still owed its
 * push (a kind with a push leg, not pushed, younger than push_owed_minutes) is older than that; `mailbox` while the beat
 * is fresh and the mailbox was last read longer ago than that; `ok` otherwise. A row past its push's bound counts for
 * nothing any more, so the state clears by itself once the push server is back. `since` is the earliest late time, or the
 * clock's when there is none (a watcher that never beat, a mailbox never read).
 */
export async function channelHealth(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "config">): Promise<ChannelHealth> {
  if (deps.config.NOTIFY === "off") return { channel: "off", since: null };
  const [row] = await deps.apiDb.execute<{ now: string; beat_at: string | null; mailbox_ok_at: string | null; owed_since: string | null; beat_late: boolean; owed_late: boolean; mailbox_late: boolean }>(sql`
    select now() as now, s.beat_at, s.mailbox_ok_at, o.owed_since,
           (s.beat_at is null or s.beat_at < now() - make_interval(mins => r.channel_down_minutes)) as beat_late,
           coalesce(o.owed_since < now() - make_interval(mins => r.channel_down_minutes), false) as owed_late,
           (s.mailbox_ok_at is null or s.mailbox_ok_at < now() - make_interval(mins => r.channel_down_minutes)) as mailbox_late
      from public.order_rules() r
      left join public.notify_state s on s.id = 1
      cross join lateral (select min(x.created_at) as owed_since from public.alert_outbox x
                           where x.pushed_at is null and x.kind = any(${words(PUSH_KINDS)})
                             and x.created_at > now() - make_interval(mins => r.push_owed_minutes)) o`);
  const at = (value: string | null) => (value === null ? null : new Date(value));
  const now = new Date(row!.now);
  if (row!.beat_late || row!.owed_late) {
    const late = [row!.beat_late ? at(row!.beat_at) : null, row!.owed_late ? at(row!.owed_since) : null].filter((d): d is Date => d !== null);
    return { channel: "down", since: late.length === 0 ? now : new Date(Math.min(...late.map((d) => d.getTime()))) };
  }
  if (row!.mailbox_late) return { channel: "mailbox", since: at(row!.mailbox_ok_at) ?? now };
  return { channel: "ok", since: null };
}

/**
 * The tick's own alarm: one row of `alert_channel_down` (mailed only) or `mailbox_unreachable` (pushed and mailed), at
 * most once in 24 hours by the outbox's own rows, with no key in the limit store. Answers whether it wrote one.
 */
async function raiseAlarm(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, kind: "alert_channel_down" | "mailbox_unreachable", since: Date): Promise<boolean> {
  const entry = ALERT_KINDS[kind];
  const facts = JSON.stringify({ since: since.toISOString() });
  const rows = await deps.apiDb.execute(sql`
    insert into public.alert_outbox (kind, priority, scope, facts)
    select ${kind}, ${entry.priority}, ${entry.scope}, ${facts}::jsonb
     where not exists (select 1 from public.alert_outbox o where o.kind = ${kind} and o.created_at > now() - make_interval(hours => 24))
    returning id`);
  return rows.length > 0;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the alert tick

export interface TickReport {
  /** How many rows alert_steps() wrote, or null when the step failed. */
  steps: number | null;
  /** How many rows the mail leg mailed. */
  mailed: number;
  /** The channel's state, or null when NOTIFY is off or the step failed. */
  channel: AlertChannelState | null;
  /** The alarms the round raised. */
  raised: ("alert_channel_down" | "mailbox_unreachable")[];
}

/**
 * One round of the alert tick (3f design, section 7.2), each step in a try of its own:
 *   1. `select alert_steps()`: the database writes every time-driven row that is due;
 *   2. the mail leg: every row of a kind whose mail is its sentence, not yet mailed and younger than
 *      ALERT_RULES.mailRetryHours, whoever wrote it, mailed to every staff account and marked when an address took it; a
 *      row nobody took is tried again next round, and then left;
 *   3. the channel's health, skipped with NOTIFY=off: its alarm rows, which the next round's mail leg mails.
 * It never mails a row of 3c's or 3e's kinds: their mails say more than the row's facts, and staffAlert sends them.
 */
export async function alertTick(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "auth" | "config" | "log">): Promise<TickReport> {
  const report: TickReport = { steps: null, mailed: 0, channel: null, raised: [] };
  const step = async (name: string, run: () => Promise<void>) => {
    try {
      await run();
    } catch (err) {
      deps.log.error({ err, job: ALERT_TICK_JOB, step: name }, "alert-tick: a step failed; the round goes on");
    }
  };

  await step("steps", async () => {
    const [row] = await deps.apiDb.execute<{ written: number }>(sql`select public.alert_steps() as written`);
    report.steps = Number(row!.written);
  });

  await step("mail", async () => {
    const rows = await deps.apiDb.execute<{ id: string; kind: StaffAlertKind; facts: AlertFacts }>(sql`
      select id, kind, facts from public.alert_outbox
       where mailed_at is null and kind = any(${words(TICK_MAILED_KINDS)})
         and created_at > now() - make_interval(hours => ${ALERT_RULES.mailRetryHours})
       order by id`);
    for (const row of rows) {
      try {
        const mailed = await mailClaimed(deps, Number(row.id), { template: row.kind, facts: row.facts });
        if (typeof mailed === "number" && mailed > 0) report.mailed++;
        else if (mailed === 0) deps.log.warn({ job: ALERT_TICK_JOB, alert: row.id, kind: row.kind }, "alert-tick: no staff address took an alert's mail; it is tried again next round");
      } catch (err) {
        deps.log.error({ err, job: ALERT_TICK_JOB, alert: row.id }, "alert-tick: an alert's mail failed; it is tried again next round");
      }
    }
  });

  if (deps.config.NOTIFY === "on") {
    await step("channel", async () => {
      const health = await channelHealth(deps);
      report.channel = health.channel;
      if (health.channel === "down" && (await raiseAlarm(deps, "alert_channel_down", health.since!))) report.raised.push("alert_channel_down");
      if (health.channel === "mailbox" && (await raiseAlarm(deps, "mailbox_unreachable", health.since!))) report.raised.push("mailbox_unreachable");
    });
  }
  return report;
}

/** The alert tick as a job of the shared lock: a round ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS after the last one ended, on one instance at a time. */
export function createAlertTick(deps: ModerationDeps, lock: JobLock) {
  return createJob({ name: ALERT_TICK_JOB, intervalMs: ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS, lockTtlMs: ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS, lock, log: deps.log, run: () => alertTick(deps) });
}
```

### Replace `apps/api/src/moderation/appeals.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { APPEALS_PAGE_SIZE, AppealsReviewedParams, DAILY_LIMITS, type AppealRequest, type AppealRow, type AppealsPage, type DecisionView } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { REDRESS_VERSION } from "@korbat/rules";
import type { ActiveStaffSession, StaffStepUpConfirmed } from "../auth";
import { isDeadlock, isLockNotAvailable } from "../lib/lock-bounds";
import { authorDecisionView, decodeListCursor, encodeListCursor } from "./author";
import { reviewerOf } from "./cases";
import { ModerationError, isModerationErrorCode, type ModerationDeps } from "./context";
import { recordConfirmed, refuseUnopened, subjectLockMode, type AnsweredFacts, type DecideOptions, type DecideOutcome } from "./decide";
import { countOrRefuse, saltedStatement } from "./intake";
import { holdsAnnouncedStanding, insertAction, insertAppeal, insertReview, pendingAppeals, raisedMessage, reviewedDecision, violatedUniqueConstraint } from "./repo";

/**
 * Appeals and their reviews (3c design, sections 6.3 and 7.7). An appeal has one shape: the author's appeal of a final
 * decision that restricts them, one for each such decision, while any of its measures is in force and within six
 * calendar months of being told. A review answers that one appeal: it keeps the decision or lifts measures of it, and
 * never restricts. The database decides whether an appeal is open and who may review it; this file inserts the rows.
 */

const DAY_MS = 24 * 60 * 60_000;

/**
 * The longest an appeal waits for a lock. Its trigger takes the case's row for the length of its own transaction and
 * waits for whoever holds the case: a decision that is being recorded, which for a seal over thousands of images is
 * seconds, or an erasure.
 */
const APPEAL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000;

/** How often the appeal's transaction is run again after a deadlock or a lock timeout: in each nothing was written. */
const APPEAL_RETRIES = 2;

/**
 * POST /api/moderation/decisions/:id/appeal: the author's appeal of a decision about their post or their account. In
 * this order:
 *   1. the day's limit, five for an account, counted before anything is read, so that whatever the answer the request
 *      was counted;
 *   2. one transaction that inserts the appeal's row. Its trigger decides, under a lock on the decision's case, whether
 *      an appeal of this decision is open now for this account (appeal_not_open: the decision is not a final
 *      restriction, is someone else's, is past its window, or nothing of it is in force), and the unique index refuses
 *      a second appeal (appeal_exists). The statement is optional and free of form; the server makes its salt and
 *      digest. A deadlock or a lock timeout runs the transaction again, and when the last run fails the same way the
 *      answer is service_unavailable;
 *   3. the answer: the decision as its author now reads it, with the appeal waiting. A decision that is not the
 *      viewer's, or of which they were not told, never opened by its id and does not now: not_found.
 * A request that failed through no fault of its sender gives its hit on the day's limit back.
 */
export async function fileAppeal(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "limits" | "log">, viewer: string, decisionId: string, request: AppealRequest): Promise<DecisionView> {
  const key = `appeal:day:account:${viewer}`;
  await countOrRefuse(deps, key, DAY_MS, DAILY_LIMITS.appeals);
  const statement = await saltedStatement(request.statement);
  try {
    for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
      try {
        await deps.apiDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
          await tx.execute(sql`select set_config('lock_timeout', ${`${APPEAL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS}ms`}::text, true)`);
          await insertAppeal(tx, { decisionId, appellantId: viewer, statement });
        });
        break;
      } catch (err) {
        const refusal = raisedMessage(err);
        if (refusal !== null && isModerationErrorCode(refusal)) throw new ModerationError(refusal);
        if (violatedUniqueConstraint(err) === "appeals_once") throw new ModerationError("appeal_exists");
        if (!isDeadlock(err) && !isLockNotAvailable(err)) throw err;
        if (attempt >= APPEAL_RETRIES) throw new ModerationError("service_unavailable", 503, undefined, 30);
      }
    }
  } catch (err) {
    // A refusal that is the sender's own (not open, appealed already) stays counted; anything else was not their doing.
    if (!(err instanceof ModerationError) || err.code === "service_unavailable") {
      await deps.limits.release(key).catch((failure: unknown) => deps.log.warn({ err: failure }, "appeal: a limit hit of a request that could not be saved could not be given back"));
    }
    throw err;
  }
  return authorDecisionView(deps, viewer, decisionId);
}

/**
 * GET /api/staff/appeals: the pending appeals, 50 a page, each marked whether the reading person may review it (3c
 * design, section 7.7). No row carries a statement: the reviewer reads it on the case page, whose read is logged and
 * counted. 3e (section 7.11 item 6): the first page lists first the appeals of a decision that holds a running suspension
 * or a termination that stands, oldest first, since the person can do nothing while they wait; then the rest, newest
 * first, which the cursor pages through. The first group is read on the first page alone, up to a page of it: as many
 * appeals of running measures as a page holds are far more than one or two staff accounts can have waiting.
 */
export async function appealsList(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, session: ActiveStaffSession, cursor?: string): Promise<AppealsPage> {
  const after = cursor === undefined ? null : decodeListCursor(cursor);
  const first = after === null ? await pendingAppeals(deps.apiDb, reviewerOf(session), null, APPEALS_PAGE_SIZE, true) : [];
  const room = APPEALS_PAGE_SIZE - first.length;
  const rest = room > 0 ? await pendingAppeals(deps.apiDb, reviewerOf(session), after, room + 1) : [];
  const page = [...first, ...rest.slice(0, room)];
  // The cursor is the last row of the rest: the first group is never paged.
  const last = rest.slice(0, room).at(-1);
  return {
    appeals: page.map(
      (row): AppealRow => ({
        id: row.id,
        caseId: row.caseId,
        decisionId: row.decisionId,
        filedAt: row.filedAt,
        decidedAt: row.decidedAt,
        deadline: row.deadline,
        ruleId: row.ruleId as AppealRow["ruleId"],
        legal: row.legal,
        actions: row.actions,
        reviewer: row.reviewer,
        needsAdmin: row.needsAdmin,
        mayReview: row.mayReview,
        standingFirst: row.standingFirst,
      }),
    ),
    // One row more than the room was read: only then is there a next page.
    nextCursor: rest.length > room && last ? encodeListCursor({ at: last.sortAt, id: last.id }) : null,
  };
}

/**
 * POST /api/staff/decisions/:decision/review, once its step-up verified (3c design, section 7.7): records the answer to
 * the author's one appeal of the decision, as a decision of kind review, in the one transaction every confirmed decision
 * runs (recordConfirmed), with its audit row as appeals_reviewed on the reviewed decision.
 *
 * Before the transaction: the redress texts are those the API serves now (the rulebook version is the reviewed
 * decision's, which the database holds the review to), and the appeal the reviewer's key confirmed is the decision's
 * pending appeal: when it is not, the appeal was answered since the console read the case, and the answer is
 * case_changed with nothing written. The database forces and compares the appeal again under the case's lock, and at
 * commit holds the audit row's params to the stored review, so a review answers exactly the appeal that was confirmed.
 * It refuses a reviewer who decided anything in the case or opened a finding in it (reviewer_conflict), a party
 * (staff_recused), and a moderator where the review needs an admin (admin_required).
 *
 * After the commit the transaction's own last step does what it does for every decision: the statement's mail, the
 * count of the person's decisions, and the mail to every staff account when the review lifted a seal.
 */
export async function review(deps: ModerationDeps, session: ActiveStaffSession, confirmed: StaffStepUpConfirmed, ctx: { requestId: string }, options: DecideOptions = {}): Promise<DecideOutcome> {
  // A confirmation of anything else never reviews an appeal: that would be a wiring fault, not a refusal.
  if (confirmed.action !== "appeals_reviewed" || confirmed.target.type !== "decision" || confirmed.keyId !== session.keyId) {
    throw new Error("a review needs a step-up that confirmed it");
  }
  const params = AppealsReviewedParams.parse(confirmed.params);
  if (params.redressVersion !== REDRESS_VERSION) throw new ModerationError("invalid_decision");
  // The routes' one list of the kinds they accept (3e design, section 7.1 item 2).
  refuseUnopened(params, options);

  const reviewsDecisionId = confirmed.target.id;
  const reviewed = await reviewedDecision(deps.apiDb, reviewsDecisionId);
  if (!reviewed) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
  if (reviewed.pendingAppealId !== params.appealId) throw new ModerationError("case_changed");
  // As for a decision: a case's target and a post's author never change, so the subject is read before the transaction.
  const subject = reviewed.target.type === "account" ? reviewed.target.id : await deps.social.postAuthor(reviewed.target.id);

  // A review holds reversals only, so its first lock stays FOR NO KEY UPDATE (3e design, section 5), a lift included,
  // but for one that keeps an announced suspension or termination in force, and so may fix its start (Task 4).
  const answered: AnsweredFacts = { kind: "review", outcome: params.outcome, holdsAnnounced: await holdsAnnouncedStanding(deps.apiDb, reviewsDecisionId) };
  return recordConfirmed(
    deps,
    session,
    confirmed,
    ctx,
    subject,
    async (tx, decisionId) => {
      await insertReview(tx, { id: decisionId, caseId: reviewed.caseId, reviewsDecisionId, decidedBy: session.userId, params });
      for (const action of params.actions) await insertAction(tx, decisionId, action);
    },
    subjectLockMode(params.actions, answered),
    reviewed.target,
  );
}

/** The case a reviewed decision belongs to, for the answer to a review that has just committed. */
export async function reviewedCase(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, decisionId: string): Promise<string> {
  const reviewed = await reviewedDecision(deps.apiDb, decisionId);
  if (!reviewed) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
  return reviewed.caseId;
}
```

```ts
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";

import { iso, rows, type Runner } from "./repo";

/**
 * The queries the author's surfaces are built from (3c design, sections 5, 7.6 and 11): the list of decisions about an
 * account, one decision's gate with the content it was made on and where its appeal stands, and the chip's facts on the
 * author's own posts. They read decisions, their ledger, cases, snapshots, the author's own appeals and posts, and the
 * database's two answers about who may review an appeal, and nothing else: no query here can reach who
 * reported, what a report said or how many there were, and a test refuses the names of those tables in this file.
 */

/** A UTC day of a timestamptz expression. The expression is written here, never input. */
const day = (expression: string) => sql.raw(`to_char(${expression} at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD')`);

/**
 * The one fragment by which every read on the author's side takes the decisions its author was told of (3f design,
 * section 5): the chip, the Cases screen, a decision's screen and the export's cases. Both halves are needed. 3c sets
 * informed_at on every decision, also on those whose author is told nothing (a report answered with "no breach"), which
 * `author_mail <> 'none'` keeps out; since 3f a decision held with an order's notice has informed_at null (and no mail),
 * which the second half keeps out, so no later change of the mail's column can show a held decision. `alias` is the
 * query's own alias of decisions, written here, never input.
 */
export const toldToAuthor = (alias: string) => sql.raw(`(${alias}.author_mail <> 'none' and ${alias}.informed_at is not null)`);

const MEASURES = sql`('withhold', 'remove', 'seal_media', 'withhold_media', 'remove_media', 'reset_display_name', 'reset_bio')`;

/**
 * The end of the appeal's window of decision `d`, while an appeal can still be filed: a final decision that restricts,
 * with at least one of its measures in force, no appeal filed, and its deadline not yet reached on the database's clock.
 * Null otherwise: for a decision taken while deciding, one that restricts nothing, a review, a correction, a restriction
 * reversed in full, and once the author appealed or the window closed. 3e Task 4: the six months run from
 * appeal_informed_at, the database's one statement of that moment, which after a kept answer to a reply sent before the
 * start is that answer's time.
 */
const appealUntil = sql`case when d.kind = 'final' and d.outcome = 'restricted'
                  and exists (select 1 from measures_in_force m where m.decision_id = d.id)
                  and not exists (select 1 from appeals ap where ap.decision_id = d.id)
                  and clock_timestamp() < public.appeal_deadline(public.appeal_informed_at(d.id))
             then ${iso("public.appeal_deadline(public.appeal_informed_at(d.id))")} end`;

/**
 * The UTC day on which the last measure of decision `d` was lifted, for a final decision that restricted and of which
 * nothing is in force any more. Null while any of its measures stands, and for every other decision: a decision taken
 * while deciding ends with its case, without a reversal.
 */
const reversedOn = sql`case when d.kind = 'final' and d.outcome = 'restricted'
                  and exists (select 1 from decision_actions a where a.decision_id = d.id and a.kind in ${MEASURES})
                  and not exists (select 1 from decision_actions a where a.decision_id = d.id and a.kind in ${MEASURES}
                                   and not exists (select 1 from decision_actions r where r.reverses_action_id = a.id))
             then (select ${day("max(r.created_at)")} from decision_actions a join decision_actions r on r.reverses_action_id = a.id where a.decision_id = d.id) end`;

/**
 * The strike decision `d` gave (3e design, section 10.2), read fresh: its end of counting, when it was overruled, and
 * whether it counts now, ran out or was overruled; all null for a decision without one.
 */
const strikeColumns = sql`(select ${iso("a.ends_at")} from decision_actions a where a.decision_id = d.id and a.kind = 'strike') as strike_until,
               (select ${iso("r.created_at")} from decision_actions a join decision_actions r on r.reverses_action_id = a.id
                 where a.decision_id = d.id and a.kind = 'strike') as strike_overruled_at,
               (select case when exists (select 1 from decision_actions r where r.reverses_action_id = a.id) then 'overruled'
                            when a.ends_at <= clock_timestamp() then 'expired' else 'counts' end
                  from decision_actions a where a.decision_id = d.id and a.kind = 'strike') as strike_state`;

/**
 * The cases about an account: the account's own, and those about the posts it wrote. A post keeps its author through its
 * deletion and the account's purge, so a decision stays with the account it was about.

const casesAbout = (accountId: string) => sql`(
    select c.id, c.target_type, c.target_id from cases c where c.target_type = 'account' and c.target_id = ${accountId}::uuid
    union all
    select c.id, c.target_type, c.target_id from cases c join posts p on p.id = c.target_id where c.target_type = 'post' and p.author_id = ${accountId}::uuid
  )`;

/** One decision as the author's list shows it. */
export interface AuthorDecisionRow {
  id: string;
  kind: "interim" | "final" | "order" | "review" | "correction";
  outcome: string;

/**
 * The author's appeal of a decision. While it is pending: whether anyone at korbat may review it now, as the database
 * answers it in one word that names nobody, and whether its review is an admin's. Once answered: its result, the UTC day
 * and the decision that answered it.

export interface AuthorAppealFacts {
  filedAt: string;

  result: "kept" | "partly_reversed" | "reversed" | null;

  answeredBy: string | null;
}

/** What the author's view of one decision adds to its statement: where its appeal stands, and its snapshot with what decides whether and how it is shown. */
export interface AuthorDecisionFacts {
  targetType: "post" | "account";

  appealUntil: string | null;
  reversedOn: string | null;

  appeal: AuthorAppealFacts | null;
  /** The database's one predicate by which a snapshot's content is withheld wherever it would be shown. */
  withheld: boolean;

  /** The UTC day the snapshot was erased; null while it is kept. */

export async function authorDecision(q: Runner, accountId: string, decisionId: string): Promise<AuthorDecisionFacts | null> {
  const [row] = await rows<Record<string, unknown>>(
    q,
    sql`select c.target_type, c.target_id, ${appealUntil} as appeal_until, ${reversedOn} as reversed_on,
               ap.id as appeal_id, ${iso("ap.filed_at")} as appeal_filed_at, public.appeal_reviewer_state(ap.id) as appeal_reviewer,
               public.review_needs_admin(d.id) as appeal_needs_admin, ap.result as appeal_result, ${day("ap.answered_at")} as appeal_answered_on,
               ap.answered_by as appeal_answered_by,
               public.snapshot_withheld(d.snapshot_id) as withheld, s.erased_at is not null as erased, ${day("s.erased_at")} as erased_on,
               exists (select 1 from decisions r join cases rc on rc.id = r.case_id
                        where rc.target_type = c.target_type and rc.target_id = c.target_id and r.redacted_at is not null) as redacted,
               s.body, s.media::text as media, coalesce(s.handle, s.author_handle) as handle, s.display_name, s.bio,
               coalesce(p.state = 'deleted_by_author', false) as post_deleted, coalesce(p.erased_at is not null, false) as post_erased,
               (c.target_type = 'post' and exists (select 1 from seal_posts sp join measures_in_force m on m.id = sp.action_id where sp.post_id = c.target_id)) as sealed,
               ${strikeColumns},
               (d.kind::text = 'order' and exists (select 1 from measures_in_force m where m.decision_id = d.id)) as order_in_force
          from decisions d
          join cases c on c.id = d.case_id
          join evidence_snapshots s on s.id = d.snapshot_id
          left join posts p on c.target_type = 'post' and p.id = c.target_id
          left join appeals ap on ap.decision_id = d.id
         where d.id = ${decisionId}::uuid and ${toldToAuthor("d")}

    reversedOn: row.reversed_on as string | null,
    appeal:
      row.appeal_id === null
        ? null
        : {
            filedAt: row.appeal_filed_at as string,
            reviewer: row.appeal_reviewer as AuthorAppealFacts["reviewer"],
            needsAdmin: row.appeal_needs_admin as boolean,
            result: row.appeal_result as AuthorAppealFacts["result"],
            answeredOn: row.appeal_answered_on as string | null,
            answeredBy: row.appeal_answered_by as string | null,
          },
    withheld: row.withheld as boolean,
    erased: row.erased as boolean,
    erasedOn: row.erased_on as string | null,
    redacted: row.redacted as boolean,
    body: row.body as string | null,
    images: row.media === null ? [] : (JSON.parse(row.media as string) as AuthorDecisionFacts["images"]),
    handle: row.handle as string,
    displayName: row.display_name as string | null,
    bio: row.bio as string | null,
    postDeleted: row.post_deleted as boolean,
    postErased: row.post_erased as boolean,
    sealed: row.sealed as boolean,
    strike:
      row.strike_until === null
        ? null
        : { countsUntil: row.strike_until as string, state: row.strike_state as DecisionStrike["state"], overruledAt: row.strike_overruled_at as string | null },
    orderInForce: row.order_in_force as boolean,
  };
}

/**
 * The decision behind the state of each of these posts that the account wrote and that is withheld or removed (3c design,
 * section 5): the decision of the strongest post measure in force, a removal (3f: or a disabling for an order, which
 * reaches this read only as the level removed, a DSA order that does not withhold) before a withhold and the newest
 * first; or,
 * for a post that is removed only because its content was erased, with no post measure in force, the newest decision
 * whose R4 redaction it was. A post of someone else, and one that is visible, is not in the answer.
 */
export async function chipFacts(q: Runner, accountId: string, postIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, PostModeration>> {
  const facts = new Map<string, PostModeration>();
  if (postIds.length === 0) return facts;
  const found = await rows<{ post_id: string; decision_id: string; rule_id: string | null; legal: boolean; interim: boolean; strike_until: string | null; is_order: boolean }>(
    q,
    sql`select p.id as post_id, f.decision_id, f.rule_id, f.legal, f.interim,
               exists (select 1 from decisions o where o.id = f.decision_id and o.kind::text = 'order') as is_order,
               -- 3e: the strike of the chip's decision while it stands and still counts.
               (select ${iso("a.ends_at")} from decision_actions a where a.decision_id = f.decision_id and a.kind = 'strike' and a.ends_at > clock_timestamp()
                   and not exists (select 1 from decision_actions r where r.reverses_action_id = a.id)) as strike_until
          from posts p
          cross join lateral (
            (select d.id as decision_id, d.rule_id, d.ground is not distinct from 'illegal' as legal, d.kind = 'interim' as interim, 0 as source,
                    (m.kind::text in ('remove', 'disable_by_order')) as removes, d.decided_at
               from measures_in_force m join decisions d on d.id = m.decision_id
              where m.post_id = p.id and m.kind::text in ('withhold', 'remove', 'disable_by_order') and ${toldToAuthor("d")})
            union all
            (select d.id, d.rule_id, d.ground is not distinct from 'illegal', false, 1, true, d.redacted_at
               from cases c join decisions d on d.case_id = c.id
              where c.target_type = 'post' and c.target_id = p.id and p.erased_at is not null and d.redacted_at is not null and ${toldToAuthor("d")}
                and exists (select 1 from decision_actions a where a.decision_id = d.id and a.kind = 'remove'))
            order by source, removes desc, decided_at desc, decision_id desc
            limit 1
          ) f
         where p.id = any(${`{${postIds.join(",")}}`}::uuid[]) and p.author_id = ${accountId}::uuid and p.moderation_level in ('withheld', 'removed')`,
  );
  for (const row of found) {
    facts.set(row.post_id, { decisionId: row.decision_id, ruleId: row.rule_id as RuleId | null, legal: row.legal, interim: row.interim, strikeUntil: row.strike_until, ...(row.is_order ? { order: true } : {}) });
  }
  return facts;
}
```

```ts
import {
  AUTHOR_CASES_PAGE_SIZE,
  mediaPath,
  type AuthorCasesPage,
  type DecisionAppeal,
  type DecisionContent,
  type DecisionStatement,
  type DecisionView,
  type ExportFormat,
  type OrderTexts,
  type PostModeration,
  type RuleId,
} from "@korbat/contracts";
import { authorDecision, authorDecisions, chipFacts, type AuthorAppealFacts, type AuthorDecisionFacts, type AuthorDecisionRow } from "./author-repo";
import { ModerationError, type ModerationDeps } from "./context";
import { decisionStatement } from "./statement";
import { orderNoticeOf } from "./statement-repo";
import { decisionStandingView, reportingStandingView } from "./standing";
import { activeStrikesOf } from "./standing-repo";

/**
 * What the author of a post or the holder of an account reads about korbat's decisions on it (3c design, sections 7.6 and
 * 10): the list of decisions they were told of, one decision with its statement's data and the content it was made on,
 * the same decisions as their export lists them (section 7.11), and the facts behind the chip on their own post.
 * Everything here is built from the author's queries and the statement's
 * data, neither of which can reach a report: an author learns the source of a decision as a category, and nothing else
 * about who reported or how often.
 */

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- page cursors

const CURSOR_TIME = /^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}[.][0-9]{6}Z$/;
const CURSOR_ID = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/;

/** Where a page of one of the app's moderation lists starts: after the row with this time (to the microsecond, as text) and id. */
export interface ListCursor {
  at: string;
  id: string;
}

/** A list's cursor: the last row's sort key as an opaque word. */
export const encodeListCursor = (cursor: ListCursor): string => Buffer.from(JSON.stringify([cursor.at, cursor.id]), "utf8").toString("base64url");

/** Reads a cursor back; anything this module did not write is refused, never guessed at. */
export function decodeListCursor(cursor: string): ListCursor {
  let parts: unknown;
  try {
    parts = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(cursor, "base64url").toString("utf8"));
  } catch {
    throw new ModerationError("invalid_request");
  }
  if (!Array.isArray(parts) || parts.length !== 2) throw new ModerationError("invalid_request");
  const [at, id] = parts as unknown[];
  if (typeof at !== "string" || !CURSOR_TIME.test(at) || typeof id !== "string" || !CURSOR_ID.test(id)) throw new ModerationError("invalid_request");
  return { at, id };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the list

/** GET /api/moderation/cases: the decisions about the viewer's account that they were told of, newest first, 20 a page. */
export async function authorCases(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, viewer: string, cursor?: string): Promise<AuthorCasesPage> {
  const after = cursor === undefined ? null : decodeListCursor(cursor);
  const found = await authorDecisions(deps.apiDb, viewer, after, AUTHOR_CASES_PAGE_SIZE + 1);
  const page = found.slice(0, AUTHOR_CASES_PAGE_SIZE);
  const last = page.at(-1);
  return {
    decisions: page.map((row) => ({
      id: row.id,
      kind: row.kind,
      outcome: row.outcome as AuthorCasesPage["decisions"][number]["outcome"],
      decidedOn: row.decidedOn,
      post: row.post,
      actions: row.actions,
      endedInterim: row.endedInterim,
      ruleId: row.ruleId as RuleId | null,
      legal: row.legal,
      appealUntil: row.appealUntil,
      reversedOn: row.reversedOn,
      appeal: row.appeal,
      strike: row.strike,
      // 3e Task 5: what a row says of a restriction of reporting and of the measures a reversal ended; absent where none.
      ...(row.reportingDays !== null ? { reportingDays: row.reportingDays } : {}),
      ...(row.endedStanding.length > 0 ? { endedStanding: row.endedStanding } : {}),
      // 3e's review (people7): a suspension's or a termination's own words, and a lift's or a withdrawal's.
      ...(row.standingMeasure !== null ? { standingMeasure: row.standingMeasure } : {}),
      ...(row.liftedStanding !== null ? { liftedStanding: row.liftedStanding } : {}),
      // 3f: an order's notice, or the reinstatement after one, names no rule.
      ...(row.order !== null ? { order: row.order } : {}),
    })),
    // One row more than the page was read: only then is there a next page.
    nextCursor: found.length > AUTHOR_CASES_PAGE_SIZE && last ? encodeListCursor({ at: last.sortAt, id: last.id }) : null,
    // The block "Your standing" above the list: the strikes that count now.
    activeStrikes: await activeStrikesOf(deps.apiDb, viewer),
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- one decision

/**
 * The content a decision was made on, or the reason it is not shown; the first that applies, in this order (3c design,
 * section 10). The database's one predicate says whether the snapshot's content may be shown at all. Where it may not,
 * an R4 redaction of the post or the account is named before a plain erasure: content that was erased because it
 * doxxed someone is said to be gone for that reason, whichever decision is viewed. A snapshot withheld without being
 * erased is one whose post's content was erased since, which only a redaction does.
 */
function contentOf(facts: AuthorDecisionFacts): DecisionContent {
  if (facts.withheld) {
    if (facts.redacted || !facts.erased || facts.erasedOn === null) return { kind: "r4_redacted" };
    return { kind: "erased", contentErasedOn: facts.erasedOn, postKept: facts.targetType === "post" && !facts.postDeleted && !facts.postErased };
  }
  if (facts.targetType === "account") return { kind: "account", handle: facts.handle, displayName: facts.displayName ?? "", bio: facts.bio ?? "" };
  // A sealed image is shown to nobody, its author included, and an image of a post its author deleted is kept for the
  // case and served to nobody: for either, the answer carries how many there are and nothing of them. Otherwise the
  // author's own image route serves each image, a withheld or removed one too; an image whose description the snapshot
  // does not hold was erased before the copy was taken, and is not listed.
  const imagesHidden = facts.sealed ? "sealed" : facts.postDeleted ? "deleted_by_author" : null;
  const images =
    imagesHidden === null
      ? facts.images.flatMap((image) => (image.alt === null ? [] : [{ id: image.id, alt: image.alt, width: image.width, height: image.height, small: mediaPath(image.id, "small"), large: mediaPath(image.id, "large") }]))
      : [];
  return { kind: "post", body: facts.body ?? "", deletedByAuthor: facts.postDeleted, images, imageCount: facts.images.length, imagesHidden };
}

/**
 * The author's appeal as their screen shows it (3c design, section 7.7). A pending appeal says whether anyone may review
 * it now and whether its review is an admin's, in the database's own two answers, which name nobody. An answered one
 * carries the statement of the decision that answered it: the review, or the correction that reversed everything before
 * a review came, read as every statement is and so told to the author in the same words as its mail.
 */
async function appealOf(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, appeal: AuthorAppealFacts): Promise<DecisionAppeal> {
  if (appeal.answeredBy === null || appeal.result === null || appeal.answeredOn === null) {
    // An appeal that is not answered always has a reviewer state: the database answers null only for an answered one.
    return { state: "pending", filedAt: appeal.filedAt, reviewer: appeal.reviewer ?? "none_eligible", needsAdmin: appeal.needsAdmin };
  }
  const answer = await decisionStatement(deps.apiDb, appeal.answeredBy);
  if (!answer) throw new Error("an appeal is answered by a decision that does not exist");
  return { state: "answered", filedAt: appeal.filedAt, answeredOn: appeal.answeredOn, result: appeal.result, answeredBy: appeal.answeredBy, statement: answer.statement };
}

/**
 * GET /api/moderation/decisions/:id: one decision as its author reads it, or not_found: for an id that names no
 * decision, for a decision about someone else, and for one its author was not told of.
 */
export async function authorDecisionView(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb"> & Partial<Pick<ModerationDeps, "config">>, viewer: string, decisionId: string): Promise<DecisionView> {
  const facts = await authorDecision(deps.apiDb, viewer, decisionId);
  if (!facts) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
  const found = await decisionStatement(deps.apiDb, decisionId, deps.config?.HOME_STATE ?? null);
  if (!found) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
  // 3f (section 10.4): an order's notice is read fresh, with the authority's words; the post is never shown while the
  // order's measure stands. Task 4 builds the erasure at the preservation's end, so no erasure is named yet.
  const notice = found.statement.order ? await orderNoticeOf(deps.apiDb, decisionId, deps.config?.HOME_STATE ?? null) : null;
  return {
    id: decisionId,
    ...found.statement,
    appealUntil: facts.appealUntil,
    reversedOn: facts.reversedOn,
    content: facts.orderInForce ? null : contentOf(facts),
    ...(notice !== null ? { orderTexts: notice.texts, erasedOn: null } : {}),
    appeal: facts.appeal === null ? null : await appealOf(deps, facts.appeal),
    strike: facts.strike,
    // 3e Task 4: where the decision's suspension or termination stands now, beside the statement that never changes.
    standing: await decisionStandingView(deps.apiDb, decisionId),
    // 3e Task 5: and where its restriction of reporting stands now.
    reportingStanding: await reportingStandingView(deps.apiDb, decisionId),
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the export's decisions

/** A decision as the account's export lists it. */
export type ExportedDecision = ExportFormat["moderation"]["decisions"][number];

/** How many decisions the export reads at a time: one statement for the page, and then each decision's statement. */
const EXPORT_PAGE_SIZE = 100;

/**
 * One decision as the export writes it (3c design, section 7.11), from the two things its author's screens are built
 * from: its row in the list and its statement's data. So the entry holds what those screens show and nothing they do
 * not: the facts and the reason of a decision that restricted nothing are not in the statement's data, and a text that
 * was erased is null there. A statement names its source as a category; the entry does not carry even that.
 */
export function exportedDecision(row: Pick<AuthorDecisionRow, "id" | "decidedOn" | "post" | "appeal">, statement: DecisionStatement, texts: OrderTexts | null = null): ExportedDecision {
  return {
    id: row.id,
    decidedOn: row.decidedOn,
    // The entry of the export's `posts` a decision about a post concerns: a post keeps its row through its deletion.
    postId: row.post?.id ?? null,
    kind: statement.kind,
    outcome: statement.outcome,
    ground: statement.ground,
    ruleId: statement.ruleId,
    rulesVersion: statement.rulesVersion,
    measures: statement.measures.map((measure) => ({ kind: measure.kind, mediaId: measure.mediaId, noEffect: measure.noEffect })),
    reversals: statement.reversals.map((reversal) => ({ kind: reversal.kind, mediaId: reversal.mediaId })),
    facts: statement.facts,
    reason: statement.reason,
    legalReference: statement.legalReference,
    appeal: row.appeal === null ? null : row.appeal === "pending" ? { state: "pending", result: null } : { state: "answered", result: row.appeal },
    // 3f (W.7): an order's notice as its facts, with the authority's words read at the export's time.
    ...(statement.order ? { order: statement.order, ...(texts ? { orderTexts: texts } : {}), erasedOn: null } : {}),
  };
}

/**
 * The export's `decisions` (ModerationForAccount.exportFor): every decision about the account that its Cases screen
 * lists, which are those its author was told of, newest first as the screen lists them. Read through the list's own
 * query, a page at a time, and each decision's statement through the statement's own read, so no decision the author was
 * not told of, and nothing a statement does not tell, can be in an export.
 */
export async function exportedDecisions(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, accountId: string): Promise<ExportedDecision[]> {
  const exported: ExportedDecision[] = [];
  let after: ListCursor | null = null;
  for (;;) {
    const page: AuthorDecisionRow[] = await authorDecisions(deps.apiDb, accountId, after, EXPORT_PAGE_SIZE);
    for (const row of page) {
      const found = await decisionStatement(deps.apiDb, row.id);
      // A decision is a row for good: one the list has just named has a statement.
      if (!found) throw new Error("a decision in its author's list has no statement");
      const notice = found.statement.order ? await orderNoticeOf(deps.apiDb, row.id, null) : null;
      exported.push(exportedDecision(row, found.statement, notice?.texts ?? null));
    }
    const last = page.at(-1);
    // A page that is not full is the last one.
    if (page.length < EXPORT_PAGE_SIZE || !last) return exported;
    after = { at: last.sortAt, id: last.id };
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the chip

/**
 * ModerationForSocial.authorFacts: for each of these posts that the viewer wrote and that is withheld or removed, the
 * decision its chip names. One query a page, asked only when the viewer wrote some of the page's restricted posts.
 */
export function authorFacts(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, viewer: string, postIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, PostModeration>> {
  return chipFacts(deps.apiDb, viewer, postIds);
}
```

```ts
/** A reply as the case page shows it: its text while korbat keeps it, which an erasure blanks. */
const replyOf = (reply: ReplyColumns | undefined): CaseDecisionAction["reply"] =>
  reply === undefined ? null : { filedAt: reply.filedAt, onTime: reply.onTime, text: reply.erasedAt === null ? reply.text : null, answeredAt: reply.answeredAt, answeredBy: reply.answeredBy };

/**
 * The queue and the case, for staff (3c design, section 7.3): the overview the home screen shows, the queue, the case
 * answer, the one door to a case's images, a fresh snapshot, and a moderator's own finding. Every read of a case is
 * written to the access log and counts against the day's limit; none of it needs the key.
 */

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the day, and the bands of a reporter's summary

/** How many seconds are left to midnight UTC, at least one: what a refusal at a daily limit tells the console to wait. */
export function secondsToUtcMidnight(now: Date): number {
  const midnight = Date.UTC(now.getUTCFullYear(), now.getUTCMonth(), now.getUTCDate() + 1);
  return Math.max(1, Math.ceil((midnight - now.getTime()) / 1000));
}

/** The same moment `months` calendar months later in UTC; a day the target month lacks becomes that month's last day. */
function monthsAfter(at: Date, months: number): Date {
  const month = at.getUTCMonth() + months;
  const lastDay = new Date(Date.UTC(at.getUTCFullYear(), month + 1, 0)).getUTCDate();
  return new Date(Date.UTC(at.getUTCFullYear(), month, Math.min(at.getUTCDate(), lastDay), at.getUTCHours(), at.getUTCMinutes(), at.getUTCSeconds(), at.getUTCMilliseconds()));
}

/** A reporter's account age as a band: under one month, one to twelve months (both ends included), or over twelve. */
export function accountAgeBand(createdAt: Date, now: Date): NonNullable<SourceSummary["accountAge"]> {
  if (now.getTime() < monthsAfter(createdAt, 1).getTime()) return "under_1_month";
  return now.getTime() <= monthsAfter(createdAt, 12).getTime() ? "1_to_12_months" : "over_12_months";
}

/** How many items a reporter filed, the one being read included, as a band. */
export function itemsFiledBand(filed: number): NonNullable<SourceSummary["itemsFiled"]> {
  if (filed <= 1) return "1";
  return filed <= 9 ? "2_to_9" : "10_or_more";
}

/** The share of a reporter's decided items that were acted on, as a band; exactly half is "half or more". */
export function actedOnBand(decided: number, actedOn: number): NonNullable<SourceSummary["actedOn"]> {
  if (decided <= 0) return "none_decided";
  if (actedOn <= 0) return "none";
  return actedOn * 2 < decided ? "under_half" : "half_or_more";
}

/** How many of a reporter's items were answered while nobody could open the images, as a band; they are counted apart from the decided ones. */
export function answeredUnseenBand(unseen: number): NonNullable<SourceSummary["answeredUnseen"]> {
  if (unseen <= 0) return "none";
  if (unseen === 1) return "1";
  return unseen <= 9 ? "2_to_9" : "10_or_more";
}

/**
 * Each reporter's place among the reporters of one case, from 0, in the order of each one's first item in the case: the
 * letter the case page gives them. Given per case, so one person's letter on one case says nothing about another.
 */
export function reporterIndexes(reportersInItemOrder: readonly (string | null)[]): Map<string, number> {
  const indexes = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const reporter of reportersInItemOrder) if (reporter !== null && !indexes.has(reporter)) indexes.set(reporter, indexes.size);
  return indexes;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- recusal

/**
 * Refuses a staff account that is too close to the case's subject: every route that names a case, or an item of one,
 * asks this first, so a refused read writes no access row and does not count against the day's limit. The check never
 * looks at who reported, and its answer reads the same whoever the conflict concerns.
 */
export async function refuseRecused(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, session: ActiveStaffSession, caseId: string): Promise<void> {
  if (await staffCaseConflict(deps.apiDb, session.userId, caseId)) throw new ModerationError("staff_recused");
}

/** The case, after the recusal check; not_found when no case has the id. */
async function openableCase(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, session: ActiveStaffSession, caseId: string): Promise<CaseRow> {
  await refuseRecused(deps, session, caseId);
  const row = await caseById(deps.apiDb, caseId);
  if (!row) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
  return row;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the overview

/** The reading person as the review marks ask about them: the session's account, and whether its role is admin. */
export const reviewerOf = (session: ActiveStaffSession) => ({ id: session.userId, admin: session.role === "admin" });

/** How long the overview's late erasures are kept before they are read again. */
export const ERASURE_OVERDUE_TTL_MS = 60_000;

/** The late erasures last read on a pool, and when: one read serves every staff member's home screen for a minute. */
const lateByPool = new WeakMap<object, { at: number; counts: Promise<ErasureOverdue> }>();

/**
 * The overview's erasureOverdue (3c design, section 7.3): one count for each due rule of what a step of the retention
 * job or the auth janitor should have changed more than a day ago and has not. The image rows are the media module's to
 * count and the notifiers' contacts the auth module's, since this module names neither.
 *
 * The counts are read at most once a minute for all staff, and a read in flight is shared: the count of late image rows
 * reads the freeze once for each kept row of a frozen account's deleted posts (seconds at twenty thousand rows), which a
 * home screen must not pay on every load, and both jobs run only every ten minutes, so a count a minute old says the
 * same. A read that failed is not kept.
 */
export function erasureOverdue(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "media" | "auth" | "now">): Promise<ErasureOverdue> {
  const now = deps.now().getTime();
  const kept = lateByPool.get(deps.apiDb);
  if (kept && now >= kept.at && now - kept.at < ERASURE_OVERDUE_TTL_MS) return kept.counts;
  const counts = (async (): Promise<ErasureOverdue> => {
    const late = await lateErasures(deps.apiDb, RETENTION);
    return { ...late, images: await deps.media.overdueDeletions(), contacts: await deps.auth.overdueContacts() };
  })();
  lateByPool.set(deps.apiDb, { at: now, counts });
  counts.catch(() => {
    if (lateByPool.get(deps.apiDb)?.counts === counts) lateByPool.delete(deps.apiDb);
  });
  return counts;
}

/**
 * GET /api/staff/overview: counts, times, staff handles and cases, for every staff member's home screen. One number is

export async function overview(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "config" | "media" | "auth" | "now">, session: ActiveStaffSession): Promise<StaffOverview> {
  const q = deps.apiDb;

  const mails = await mailAndReleaseCounts(q, RETENTION.mailGiveUpDays);
  const appeals = await appealCounts(q, reviewerOf(session));
  return {
    lanes: ([0, 1, 2] as const).map((lane) => byLane.find((row) => row.lane === lane) ?? { lane, open: 0, oldestAt: null }),
    appealsWaiting: appeals.waiting,
    appealsYouMayReview: appeals.mayReview,
    appealsWithoutReviewer: appeals.withoutReviewer,

    imagesToday: today.images,

    releaseOverdue: mails.releaseOverdue,
    erasureOverdue: await erasureOverdue(deps),

    // The three lists of the path for child sexual abuse material, which every staff member sees: what lifted the
    // protection of reported images, who chose not to seal, and which seals taken while deciding stand.
    protectionLifted: await recentProtectionLifted(q, OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX),
    sealsDeclined: await recentSealsDeclined(q, OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX),
    interimSeals: await interimSealsInForce(q, OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX),

    repliesWaiting: await repliesWaiting(q),

/** StaffOverview.alerts: the channel's state as the tick judges it, with the time since when. */
```
